messages:
mina: FYI — seeing intermittent JSON schema violations from the int8 streaming canary. Looks like chunks sometimes arrive out-of-order and get concatenated, resulting in mid-object insertion and parse failures. Repro steps below.

jordan: repro reliably? what input/flags?

mina: can repro ~1/200 requests on my laptop when forcing parallel frame delivery. Canary: raven-lite-int8, streaming enabled, structured-output route. Logs show chunk seq inversion: 

```
[canary] recv chunk seq=2 model=raven-lite-int8 stream_id=abcd token_count=12
[canary] recv chunk seq=1 model=raven-lite-int8 stream_id=abcd token_count=8
[canary] merged buffer => "..., \"tool_call\": { \"name\": \"search\",\"
```

(you can see seq=2 got merged before seq=1 -> partial JSON then another chunk appended)

sam_k: hmm are we assigning sequence numbers on the wire? we normally rely on websocket frame ordering. any proxy or gateway between model and aggregator?

opsbot: deploy-proxy reported a transient 503s window for shard-4 at 2024-09-18T14:02:11Z (incident INF-3419), see https://internal/ops/INF-3419 :warning:

lia_p: saw something similar in a production edge-proxy rollout last month. Aggregator will append frames as they arrive; if multiple backends decode in parallel we can get interleaving. Might be a race in the collector where we merge buffers without per-stream sequence checks.

mina: hypothesis: streaming chunker flushes on token thresholds and EOS; ensemble parallel decoders return their chunks independently. Aggregator uses arrival order rather than explicit sequence metadata. Fix options: attach chunk sequence+stream-id at wire-level and reorder client-side, or make chunk boundaries atomic (no interleaving for structured-output routes).

andre: short-term mitigation: update schema validator to be more tolerant: buffer until full JSON object detected (matching braces) and attempt incremental parses/rescue. That reduces customer impact but hides the root cause.

jordan: suggested action list?

mina: proposed: 
1) push a repro harness that interleaves frames deterministically (I have one) and put it in eng-ml/canary-repro/stream-reorder.sh
2) add a seq header to stream frames (wire change) and have aggregator sort per stream_id before merging
3) temporary canary config: disable streaming for structured-output routes for int8 quant canaries until wire fix ships
4) telemetry: increment malformed_json counter with tags model, route, canary_run_id to measure regression impact

sam_k: I'll draft PR to add seq header + aggregator sort by seq. Also add a feature-flag to disable streaming per-route.

lia_p: I'll add CI fuzz test that randomizes interleaving order and asserts final concatenation is valid NDJSON/JSON per route. Test name: streaming_interleave_fuzz.

mina: thanks. I'll upload the repro gist and post the exact commands. Also we should decide whether to backport fix to dedicated runtime v1.12.

opsbot: Created ticket INF-3421 and linked INF-3419. Assigned to sam_k, lia_p. https://internal/ops/INF-3421 :white_check_mark:

andre: quick note — prefer seq header field `x-stream-seq` (int) + `x-stream-id` (uuid). Keep fallback to arrival order if headers absent to avoid breaking older runtimes.

mina: agreed. small todo: update docs for structured-output streaming best-practices.

jordan: thanks team :thumbsup: I'll follow up in the PR review.

mina: uploading repro now, will ping when done :mag:
